name: Cyberdesk

modes.label: Native product; see regime notes
modes.note: Not a compute rental: Cyberdesk hosts no VMs. Customers install the Cyberdriver agent on their OWN physical or virtual Windows machines; Cyberdesk bills per automation step (agentic steps and cheaper cached/replayed steps) at contract-specific rates. Steps are billed for success, user-task-failed and cancelled runs; infrastructure failures are not billed. No per-vCPU/GiB/hour rate exists, so rates stay null.

caveats: Public desktop automation API product with demo-led sales; /pricing renders only headline even in Chrome. No verified hosted OS hardware size, tariff or CPU-hour rate. Windows desktop use is lead evidence, not guaranteed purchasable Windows VM configuration.
Null values mean unknown, not free/unlimited. No model-token cost, tax or unverified ancillary charge included.
Native browser/device/task/credit prices with unknown CPU/RAM are deliberately non-priceable. Check regime before interpreting any partial resource estimate.

Cyberdesk is a computer-use AGENT platform, not a machine host: every machine is customer-supplied (Cyberdriver on your own Windows PC/VM), billed per agentic/cached step at contract rates; no public price, self-serve is a waitlist. Any Windows VM cost is paid separately to the customer's own cloud. Consider excluding it from compute rankings or keeping the mode 'alt' with all rates null.
API rate limits: dashboard JWT traffic 480 requests/user and 4,000 requests/org per 60-second window; public API-key limits separate and unpublished; raise by emailing the founders.

snapshot_auto.quote: Provision Windows: Use Windows Server 2022 or a supported Windows desktop environment. RDP is useful for initial setup, but Cyberdriver should continue working after RDP disconnects.
snapshot_auto.note: Cyberdesk hosts no machines. You provision your own Windows PC/VM and install Cyberdriver (a RustDesk-based tunnel agent). Machine lifecycle and snapshots belong to your own cloud or hypervisor.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: The Cyberdriver CLI is useful when you bake a Windows AMI or golden template, then clone many VMs from it. The main rule is simple: install Cyberdriver in the image, but connect each cloned VM with its own API key and identity when it first boots.
snapshot_on_demand.note: No first-party snapshot API. Golden images and AMIs are made in your own cloud. The docs' 'trajectories' (recorded action replays) and 'workflow duplication' are not machine snapshots.

own_agent_api.quote: This guide will walk you through creating your first workflow, installing Cyberdriver, and executing a run programmatically.
own_agent_api.note: Cyberdesk's own computer-use agent only. The REST API plus TS/Python SDKs let you create runs (workflow prompt plus inputs, per-run prompt/model overrides), bulk runs, run chains on a reserved machine session, retry, get run messages/screenshots/attachments, and receive run_complete webhooks. The agent runs in Cyberdesk's cloud and drives the desktop through the Cyberdriver tunnel, not inside the machine. No token streaming or third-party harnesses (Claude Code, Codex) documented.

egress_allowlist.quote: Cyberdriver connects outbound to Cyberdesk over HTTPS/WebSocket. Some organizations need that traffic to go through a company-controlled domain for firewall allowlisting or traffic inspection.
egress_allowlist.note: The machine and its network are yours. Egress control is your own firewall or cloud security groups. Cyberdesk offers no per-machine egress policy, only guidance on routing Cyberdriver's own tunnel through your proxy.

egress_http_rules.note: Not a machine host. No first-party network policy of any kind.

guest_firewall.note: Your own Windows machine with Administrator (the installer requires admin), so Windows Defender Firewall / netsh rules apply. nftables/iptables don't apply (Windows).

secret_proxy.quote: Sensitive values are stored in a secure vault during the run, never logged or sent to LLMs, resolved only during actual computer actions, and deleted immediately after the run completes.
secret_proxy.note: Sensitive inputs and desktop parameters ({$password}, stored in Basis Theory) are hidden from the LLM and logs but are typed or used on the desktop itself, so the secret does enter the machine. Not an outbound credential-injecting proxy.

volume_attach.quote: Use Windows Server 2022 or a supported Windows desktop environment.
volume_attach.note: No hosted machines, so no first-party volumes. Disks are whatever your own VM/PC has. Files move via the file read/write API and run attachments.

volume_shared.note: No first-party shared storage. Run attachments and prompt images live in Cyberdesk storage and are fetched via signed URLs, not mounted.
